member.name: T:Supabase.Core.Diagnostics.ActivityExtensions
member.summary:
Null-safe helpers for tagging activities with OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions.
All members accept a null (the result of when nothing is listening) and no-op, so call sites need no listener checks. URLs are recorded through only — never record a raw URL, query string, token, or other credential as a tag value.

member.summary: Tags an outgoing HTTP request following OpenTelemetry HTTP client conventions. The URL is sanitized to scheme/host/port/path; the query string is never recorded.
member.param: The activity to tag, or null when nothing is listening.
The request URI, sanitized before tagging.

member.name: T:Supabase.Core.Diagnostics.Instrumentation
member.summary:
Factory methods for the and instances used by the Supabase client libraries.
Emission is zero-cost unless a consumer subscribes a listener (e.g. via the OpenTelemetry SDK with AddSource("Supabase.*") / AddMeter("Supabase.*")), so instrumentation built on these sources is always on and requires no configuration to stay silent.

member.name: T:Supabase.Core.Diagnostics.UrlSanitizer
member.summary:
Reduces URLs to a form that is safe to record in telemetry and logs.
Supabase URLs routinely carry secrets outside the path — access tokens in fragments, API keys, PKCE verifiers and grant parameters in query strings — so telemetry must only ever record scheme, host, port and path. There is no overload that keeps the query string; that is deliberate.

member.name: M:Supabase.Core.Diagnostics.UrlSanitizer.Sanitize(System.Uri)
member.summary: Returns scheme://host[:port]/path for the given URI, dropping user info, the query string, and the fragment. Default ports are omitted.
member.param: The URI to reduce to scheme, host, port and path.

member.name: M:Supabase.Core.Diagnostics.UrlSanitizer.Sanitize(System.String)
member.summary: Sanitizes a URL provided as a string; returns the input truncated at the first query/fragment delimiter when it cannot be parsed as a URI.
member.param: The URL to sanitize; parsed as an absolute URI when possible.
